status: Calibrated for 103 ordinary tasks in eight lanes plus seven browser tasks; three warm samples and one explicit dependency-cache-miss sample.

calibration.method: Maximum successful observation in each cache profile plus 20% headroom, rounded up to five minutes or one GiB.

notes: These are regression-reporting thresholds for the recorded task/lane/browser inventory, not the faster feedback targets in the development-workflow plan.
The cost command reports budget_met; a cost overrun alone does not fail the required correctness gate.
Feedback includes queue and setup through required completion. Aggregate cost sums job wall time, not billable price.
Warm requires every configured GitHub cache to restore its matching key. Cold disables GitHub restores and saves; both retain upstream Nix substitutes.
Restored bytes sum GitHub transfers across jobs, exclude upstream Nix traffic and are distinct from repository cache occupancy.
Failed, incomplete, cancelled, scoped or unknown-cache results cannot calibrate a passing full-suite budget.
Three warm observations provide an initial baseline, not a statistical tail guarantee. One cold sample does not establish cold variance.
A changed scenario inventory or lane allocation requires explicit recalibration. Historical 33-task limits remain attributed separately.
No paid runner, cache quota increase or weaker scenario deadline is selected by these budgets.
An inventory hash checks task and lane registration, not every internal assertion or workload size. Source, toolchain and workload changes still need review before attributing a timing difference.

targets.status: Uncalibrated implementation targets; successful comparable hosted runs must establish the improvement.

regressions.confirmation: Two consecutive comparable successful runs; comparison includes inventory, cache profile and runner labels.
